Case Information.Type of Document: Letter of Acceptance, Waiver, and Consent (AWC)

OverallSummary: This case involves Nicholas Michael Caruso's willful violation of Regulation Best Interest's Care Obligation (Rule 15l-1 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934) and FINRA Rule 2010 by excessively trading in the accounts of two retail customers between September 2022 and May 2023. Both customers were in their early sixties with similar financial profiles (income between $100,000-$200,000 and liquid net worth between $200,000-$500,000). The excessive trading was determined through analysis of two key metrics: 1) cost-to-equity ratios that significantly exceeded the 20% threshold that generally indicates excessive trading (49% for Customer A and 30% for Customer B), and 2) a turnover rate of 6.56 for Customer B that exceeded the threshold of 6 that indicates excessive trading. Caruso engaged in a pattern of in-and-out, short-term trading without considering the cumulative costs. For Customer A, Caruso effected 20 trades involving purchases of approximately $146,000 in securities despite an average account balance of only $19,600, resulting in $4,500 in losses and over $7,300 in commissions and costs. For Customer B, Caruso effected 32 trades involving purchases of approximately $145,800 in securities with an average account balance of only $22,200, resulting in $15,800 in losses and over $6,800 in commissions and costs. As a result, Caruso placed his and his firm's interests ahead of his customers' interests. The AWC imposed a three-month suspension from associating with any FINRA member in all capacities, with no monetary sanctions due to Caruso's demonstrated financial inability to pay.
